senses.gloss: (b. h.), perf. חָב, part. חַיָיב, חָב [to be bound over, seized,]
to be declared guilty, be sentenced; to be punishable; to be (legally, morally or religiously) bound, to be responsible.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:1">B. Kam. I, 1</cite> <he>חב המזיק</he> he who caused the damage must pay.
Ib. 6ᵇ חב … חייב … מיבעי לה the Mishnah says ḥab, ought it not rather to read ḥayab (part.)?—[Answ.: they are the words of a Jerusalem Tannai.]—
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:2">Ib. I, 2</cite> <he>כל שׁחַבְתִּי בשמירתו וכ׳</he> for whatever I am legally bound to guard, I am legally answerable in case of injury.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:1">Sabb. I, 1</cite> <he>העני חייב</he> the recipient (the person standing outside) is guilty (of transgressing the Sabbath law).—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 1:1:7">Y. Ned. I, 36ᵈ</cite> top <he>חב על כל וכ׳</he> he is punishable for each separately.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 9:5">Ber. IX, 5</cite> <he>חייב אדם וכ׳</he> man must praise the Lord &c.
<cite ref="Chagigah 4a">Ḥag. 4ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>כל מצוה שהאשה חַיֶיבֶת בה וכ׳</he> whatever religious act is obligatory on woman, is also obligatory &c.—
<cite ref="Chagigah 4a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>מה להלן נשים חַיָיבוֹת</he> as there (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 31:12">Deut. XXXI, 12</cite>) women are included in the obligation; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to act in behalf of a person to the latter’s disadvantage.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 7:11">Erub. VII, 11</cite> <he>ואין חָבִין וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="G00443"><he>זָכָה</he></cite>. Y. B. Kam. IV, 4ᵇ bot. <he>בתחלה … ע״מ לָחוֹב להן וכ׳</he> originally guardians are not assigned to minors that they may eventually act to their disadvantage &c.; <he>ואם חָבוּ חָבוּ</he> but if they have done so, their action is legal (and they cannot be held responsible); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:4:3">Y. Gitt. V, 47ᵃ</cite> top.—
Y. Keth. XI, 34ᵇ bot. נמצאתה חב וכ׳ then you would cause a disadvantage to the relics; a. fr.—ח׳ בעצמו to be alone answerable for one’s loss.

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 1:3">Ber. I, 3</cite> <he>כדאי היית לָחוֹב בעצמך</he> thou wouldst have deserved to be made answerable &c., i.e. if you had met with an accident you would have had none but yourself to blame.
Shebu. VII, 5; a. fr.—ח׳ חטאת to be bound to bring a sin-offering; ח׳ מיתה to be subject to death penalty.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 7:1">Sabb. VII, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 11:6">Ib. XI, 6</cite> <he>כל חַיְיבֵי חטאת וכ׳</he> all those eventually bound to bring &c., are not bound, unless &c.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 58b">Snh. 58ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to declare guilty, to convict, sentence (opp. זִיכָּה, פָּטַר).
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 6a:2">Snh. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>ח׳ את הזכאי</he> if a judge (by an illegal decision) convicted one who ought to have been acquitted.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 3:6">Ib. III, 6</cite> <he>ואחד מְחַיֵּיב</he> and one votes for acquittal.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 4:13">Shebu. IV, 13</cite> <he>ר׳ מאיר מח׳ וכ׳</he> R. M. says, he is guilty (of blasphemy); a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 32">Ex. R. s. 32</cite>, beg. <he>חִיַּיבְתֶּם עצמיכם</he> you have given judgment against yourselves.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 3b:4">B. Mets. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>פיו אין מְחַיְּיבוֹ ממון וכ׳</he> the defendant’s own statement cannot cause a judgment against him to pay a penalty, but causes the imposition of an oath.
Yoma 35ᵇ הלל מח׳ וכ׳, v. הִלֵּל.—Part. pass. מְחוּיָּיב, מְחוּיָּב = חַיָיב, sentenced, bound. Y. Keth. III, 27ᵇ מְחוּיְּיבֵי מיתות those sentenced to death, מ׳ מכות sentenced to lashes.—

<cite ref="Berakhot 20b">Ber. 20ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כל שׁאינו מ׳ בדבר וכ׳</he> whatever is not obligatory upon a person himself, cannot be done by him as a representative of the community, v. <cite ref="H00242"><he>חוֹבָה</he></cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Ketubot 30b">Keth. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>מי שנ׳ סקילה</he> he who (under Jewish jurisdiction) would have been sentenced to death through stoning.
<cite ref="Ketubot 30b">Ib.</cite> <he>כבר נ׳ בגניבה וכ׳</he> he was amenable to punishment for theft, before he transgressed &c.
<cite ref="Ketubot 30b:4">Ib.</cite> <he>מִתְחַיֵּיב בנפשו לא הוה וכ׳</he> but guilty of a deadly sin he was not until he ate it; a. fr.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:4">Ab. III, 4</cite>, a. fr. <he>הרי זה מתח׳ בנפשו</he> he is responsible for his life, would have himself to blame, if any accident should befall him (v.
<cite ref="Berakhot 3a">Ber. 3</cite> quoted above).

senses.gloss: to be doomed, to have the misfortune to.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Shevuot 3:4">Tosef. Shebu. III, 4</cite> <he>אין אדם מתח׳ לשמוע וכ׳</he> one has not the misfortune to hear (a curse &c.), unless he sinned himself (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 5:1">Lev. V, 1</cite>).
<cite ref="Leviticus 5:1">Ib.</cite> <he>הרואה … עבירה נ׳ לראות</he> if one sees people sin, (we say) he had the misfortune to see, opp. <he>זכה</he>.
